The title names the standard method, not an additional theorem in its Definition. The separate prop-rkc-stability-intervals-and-stage-degree proves its polynomial, R(0)=R'(0)=1, exact interval [-2s^2,0] and self-adjoint nonexpansion by the Chebyshev recurrence. The procedure covers s=1, finite stage loops and all failure branches. Its first-order normalization also follows directly from the first-order stage coefficients c_j=j^2/s^2. Properties correctly remain separate; a reverse deps edge to its analyzing proposition would create a cycle.

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt: **Inputs.** Supply pointwise smooth data on $[0,T]$ from [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]], an original mesh, a piecewise-constant control parameterization, an explicit tableau from [[def-explicit-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-map]] or a possibly implicit tableau from [[def-ctrl1-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-collocation]], one of `single-shooting`, `multiple-shooting`, or `collocation` mode, a finite smooth representation of the control constraints when a solver-ready NLP is requested, finite sets of declared path-constraint times, endpoint constraints, the tableau quadrature rule, an initial decision vector $z_0$ and multiplier vector $\mu_0$, a stage residual tolerance $\tau_s\ge0$, a quadrature error tolerance $\tau_q\ge0$, a stage Newton correction cap $M_s\in\mathbb N_0$, and a maximum number of mesh nodes. For the direct linear-stage branch, optionally supply exact pointwise coefficient maps $A:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $B:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ satisfying $f(t,x,u)=A(t)x+B(t)u$ at every queried stage input; only this explicit representation enables that branch. Supply a deterministic derivative evaluator for the actual returned stage maps and resulting finite NLP on an open neighborhood of the queried candidate. On a locally fixed strict stopping branch of the finite stage-iteration procedure, differentiate that finite graph, including when the residual happens to be exactly zero at the queried point. Implicit differentiation as in [[thm-implicit-differentiation-forward-and-adjoint-formulas]] is permitted only when the selected returned stage map is certified to agree on that neighborhood with the exact local solution branch and its residual Jacobian is nonsingular there; an exact residual at the queried point alone does not establish this agreement. Return `derivative-failure` when no derivative of the actual returned map is available. Supply a quadrature error evaluator which returns a certified upper bound for the objective quadrature discrepancy or `unavailable`. Each supplied evaluator returns a value or failure in finite time. An optional trajectory-estimation request supplies the inputs of [[alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-controller]].
